review: 1:1–1:4 the Arabic is Matthew 18:20 (حَيْثُمَا اجْتَمَعَ اثْنَانِ … هُنَاكَ أَكُونُ); the Hebrew keeps the three nouns (קְהִלָּה, חִבּוּר, דְּבַר אֱמֶת) and the 'then' of the inference, so the stanza still argues from the promise to the presence.

3:3–3:4 אֶת־פָּנֶיךָ הָאֱמֶת … שׁוֹמֵעַ — the Arabic حُضُورَكَ الْحَقَّ … يَا سَمِيع is 'Your true presence … O Hearer'; פָּנִים is the biblical idiom for presence (Exod 33:14–15), and שׁוֹמֵעַ is kept as the divine title of Ps 65:3.

2:3–2:4 הַרְאֵה בָנוּ רָאשְׁךָ — the Arabic أَظْهِرْ بِهِ رِيَاسَتَك / فِينَا is 'show Your headship in us'; רֹאשׁ is used concretely (as in Eph 1:22, רֹאשׁ לַכֹּל) rather than the abstract Modern Hebrew מַנְהִיגוּת.

5:3 בְּפָנֶיךָ זוֹרְחֵי־נֹגַהּ — the Arabic فِي وَجْهِكَ بَاهِي السَّنَا is 'in Your face, radiant in splendour'; נֹגַהּ is the prophetic noun for brightness (Isa 4:5; Ezek 1:4), kept over the Modern Hebrew בְּהִירוּת.

5:4 דְּמוּת אֱלֹהִים עֶלְיוֹן — the Arabic يَا صُورَةَ اللهِ الْعَلِيّ is 'O image of God Most High'; the Hebrew keeps the two words of Gen 1:27 (דְּמוּת) and Num 24:16 (עֶלְיוֹן) rather than the later theological דְּמוּת אֱלֹהִית.
